title: The Ship That Wasn't Mining
narrativeQuestion: How did the CIA try to steal a sunken Soviet submarine from three miles down, and why does its answer about the mission still shape government secrecy?

chapters.title: A Submarine Disappears
chapters.claim: K-129 sank in March 1968 with 98 men and three nuclear missiles. The Soviets never found it, and USS Halibut photographed the wreck that summer.

chapters.title: Three Miles of Pipe
chapters.claim: The CIA planned to lift an object it estimated at 2,000 to 2,200 tons from 16,500 feet on a string of pipe.

chapters.title: Enter Howard Hughes
chapters.claim: Howard Hughes lent his name to a deep ocean mining cover story, and the ship sailed around South America to reach California in 1973.

namedPeople.name: Howard Hughes
namedPeople.role: billionaire who lent his name to the cover story

chapters.title: What Kind of Vessel Are You?
chapters.claim: On July 18, 1974 the Soviet ship Chazhma questioned the Glomar Explorer by radio and accepted the mining answers.

chapters.title: The Claw Breaks
chapters.claim: Part of the capture vehicle failed during the August 1974 lift, and only the forward section of K-129 reached the ship on August 8.

chapters.title: Six Sailors
chapters.claim: Six Soviet sailors were buried at sea on September 4, 1974, and Robert Gates gave the film to Boris Yeltsin in October 1992.

chapters.title: The Burglary That Blew the Cover
chapters.claim: A June 1974 burglary at Summa Corporation led to a February 1975 Los Angeles Times story and Jack Anderson's March 1975 broadcast.

namedPeople.name: William Colby
namedPeople.role: CIA Director who asked editors to hold the story

chapters.title: Neither Confirm Nor Deny
chapters.claim: The CIA's reply to Harriet Ann Phillippi's 1975 request became the Glomar response, upheld by a federal appeals court in 1976.

namedPeople.name: Harriet Ann Phillippi
namedPeople.role: Rolling Stone reporter who filed the request

accuracyNotes: The radio exchange is quoted from pages 39 and 40 of the CIA history. The alternative replies are invented choices and are labeled as not what the crew said.
Accounts disagree on whether code equipment was recovered. The hub states the disagreement instead of picking a side.
Exact break points of the hull remain classified, so the submarine drawing is labeled simplified.
